title: Prioritization orchestra for catalog requests with eval-harness hooks
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Context:
We receive a steady stream of model onboarding requests from customers and partners: new open checkpoints, custom quantized builds, and version-pin asks. Current intake funnels are ad-hoc, causing long wait times for enterprise customers and inconsistent application of eval gates. This ticket defines a prioritization 'orchestra'—a lightweight, telemetry-driven scorer that routes requests into lanes (fast-review, shadow-eval, staged-pin, standard-onboard) and emits hooks for the eval harness so we can automatically schedule targeted regressions and stability checks.

Goals:
- Define a reproducible scoring rubric that combines customer SLA, usage signal (tokens/sec, request volume), security/compliance flags, and model novelty to rank requests.
- Integrate scoring output into the catalog intake flow so requests are assigned to one of four lanes with clear SLAs.
- Add eval-harness hooks: when a request enters the shadow-eval lane, trigger a preconfigured eval job with customer-provided prompts, historical regression sets, and baseline metrics.
- Surface telemetry and decision rationale in the intake UI and create an audit log for enterprise reviewers.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Scorer prototype deployed behind a feature flag that annotates incoming requests with lane and score.
2) Shadow-eval hook successfully triggers a CI eval job that returns pass/fail and delta metrics within 2 hours for small eval packs.
3) Intake UI displays top three signals and the computed score; reviewers can override lane with an explicit justification.
4) Documentation and runbook for reviewers explaining lanes, typical time-to-resolution, and fallback paths.

Design and heuristics (proposal):
- Score components (weighting): customer_tier 35%, request_volume_estimate 20%, novelty_delta 15%, compliance_flags 20%, stability_history 10%.
- Novelty_delta computed using model architecture + tokenizer fingerprint vs catalog variants; thresholded to force full-eval for high novelty.
- Compliance flags include: external data IP risk, encryption/KMS requirement, and export-control flags. Any hard flag forces at least "staged-pin" lane.

Eval-harness integration details:
- On shadow-eval lane assignment, create evaluation run via /internal-eval-api with payload: model_variant_id, customer_prompt_suite_id, baseline_model_id.
- Eval runner must return structured metrics (latency, score, hallucination-rate, safety-checks) and a human-readable summary.
- Failure modes: if eval runner times out, escalate to manual review and place request into "staged-pin" with reduced SLA.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Deploy scorer as read-only annotations; collect telemetry for 7 days.
- Week 2: Enable lane assignment behind feature flag for 10% of requests; enable eval-harness hook only for internal test tenants.
- Week 3: Expand to enterprise beta tenants and provide reviewer training.
- Week 5: Full rollout and deprecate ad-hoc intake spreadsheet route.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overweighting customer_tier may starve non-enterprise but high-utility open model additions; mitigate by using floor-level allocation for community models.
- Eval cost: shadow-evals increase infra cost; we'll limit initial eval packs and introduce sampling heuristics for low-volume requests.

- Eval harness RFC: https://confluence.company.com/display/EVAL/Eval+Runner+API+Spec
- Mock UI screens: https://design.example.com/catalog-intake-annotated

- PM: finalize weightings and publish scoring doc (Priya).
- Eng: implement scorer endpoint + feature flag (Diego).
- Evals: add a minimal runner endpoint for automated shadow-eval (Sven).
- UX: add decision rationale UI for reviewers (Maya).
